title: Ocular Disorders Associated with Systemic Diseases

chunks.title: Retinal vs choroidal circulation & haemorrhage types
chunks.tldr: Ophthalmic artery = first ICA branch → central retinal artery + posterior ciliary arteries. Retinal: end-arterioles, tight 7 µm capillaries (inner BRB), autoregulated, no autonomic nerves. Choroidal: most of the blood flow, fenestrated 30 µm capillaries, autonomic control, collaterals. Haemorrhage by layer: preretinal/subhyaloid (boat-shaped fluid level, NV), flame (NFL), dot-blot (inner nuclear), Roth spot (white-centred — endocarditis, leukaemia, diabetes), subretinal (CNV; fuzzy border), sub-RPE (dark, sharp border). Choroidal infarcts leave Elschnig spots, Amalric triangles, Siegrist streaks. Cotton-wool spots = NFL axoplasmic stasis from precapillary arteriole occlusion; fade in ~6 weeks.
points: Isolated unexplained CWS → think diabetes, HTN, HIV, SLE, GCA, emboli.
chunks.hook: Flame = flat in the fibre layer; blot = deep, sideways-on.

cards.q: What is a Siegrist streak?
cards.a: Linear pigmented chorioretinal streak over a choroidal artery, from choroidal infarction (malignant hypertension, vasculitis).

cards.q: Causes of Roth spots?
cards.a: Bacterial endocarditis, leukaemia, anaemia, diabetes, HIV, sepsis.

chunks.title: Ocular ischaemia, emboli & CCF (systemic view)
chunks.tldr: Amaurosis fugax: three emboli — cholesterol (Hollenhorst; carotid atheroma), platelet-fibrin, calcific (aortic/mitral valve → CRAO). Under-40s/cardiac history → AF, valves, endocarditis, LV thrombus. Examine fundus, carotid bruit, heart, pulse; Doppler/echo. Incidental emboli = stroke risk. Other transient loss: GCA, hyperviscosity, anaemia, hypotension, migraine, papilloedema obscurations, gaze-evoked amaurosis (ONSM, orbital mass), UGH syndrome. Ocular ischaemic syndrome (severe carotid stenosis, Takayasu): mid-peripheral haemorrhages, MAs, CWS, NVD, NVI, low or high IOP — mistaken for DR/RVO. CCF: direct (trauma/aneurysm/EDS) vs dural (DM/HTN, often resolve); corkscrew vessels, high IOP, VI palsy, dilated SOV (≠ TED).

cards.q: Imaging feature distinguishing CCF from thyroid eye disease?
cards.a: Dilated superior ophthalmic vein (with arterialised flow) in CCF; both may show enlarged muscles.

chunks.title: Vein occlusion work-up & hypertensive retinopathy
chunks.tldr: RVO risks: age, raised IOP, HTN, smoking, DM, lipids, renal failure, collagen vascular disease, hyperviscosity (myeloma, Waldenström). Tests: FBC, ESR, renal function, lipids, glucose/HbA1c, protein electrophoresis; young → thrombophilia (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, protein C/S, APC resistance/factor V Leiden, antithrombin III, homocysteine). Ischaemic CRVO: <10% reach 6/60; non-ischaemic >80%. Hypertensive retinopathy (Mitchell-Wong): mild = arteriolar narrowing, AV nicking, copper wiring; moderate = haemorrhages, MAs, CWS, exudates (stroke risk); malignant = + disc swelling (± macular star, choroidal infarcts, exudative RD) — lower BP gradually (fast drop can infarct the nerve). Elderly sclerotic vessels protect against florid retinopathy.
chunks.hook: Disc swelling + star + haemorrhages + BP 220/140 = malignant hypertension — admit.

cards.q: What defines malignant hypertensive retinopathy in Mitchell-Wong grading?
cards.a: Moderate retinopathy signs plus optic disc swelling.

cards.q: Thrombophilia tests for a young patient with RVO?
cards.a: Lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, protein C, protein S, APC resistance/factor V Leiden, antithrombin III, homocysteine.

chunks.title: Leukaemia, hyperviscosity, sickle & paraneoplastic retinopathy
chunks.tldr: Leukaemia (esp. acute): retinal haemorrhages (Roth spots), infiltrates, disc infiltration (emergency RT), CWS. Hyperviscosity (polycythaemia, Waldenström, myeloma): dilated tortuous veins, haemorrhages, MAs — reverses with plasmapheresis. Sickle: worse in HbSC & S-thal than SS; conjunctival comma vessels, salmon patch (fresh intraretinal bleed) → iridescent spots, black sunburst; peripheral non-perfusion → sea-fan NV (often autoinfarcts; laser rarely). Hyphaema in sickle trait → IOP rises easily, avoid CAIs. Metastases: breast (women), lung (men); ⅓ have no known primary. CAR (anti-recoverin, small-cell lung) and MAR (melanoma; night blindness, negative ERG).
chunks.hook: SC disease sees worse than SS — sea fans.

cards.q: Which sickle genotype carries the highest risk of proliferative retinopathy?
cards.a: HbSC (then HbS-thalassaemia), more than HbSS.

cards.q: What is a 'black sunburst' in sickle retinopathy?
cards.a: A pigmented chorioretinal scar from resolved intraretinal/subretinal haemorrhage with RPE hyperplasia.

chunks.title: Diabetes beyond the retina
chunks.tldr: DM prevalence ~8.5% of adults; DR = commonest cause of new blindness in working age; 40–45% of US diabetics have DR. Type 1: 60–75% severe (often proliferative) DR by 20 y; type 2: maculopathy. Other eye effects: snowflake 'true diabetic' cataract (rapid, young), earlier age-related cataract, refractive swings with glucose (±3–4 D), iris glycogen → poor dilation, autonomic pupil changes, rubeosis/NVG, microvascular III/IV/VI palsy (pupil-sparing III, recovers ~3 months), NAION, diabetic papillopathy (mild chronic disc swelling).
points: Think diabetes in any unexplained retinopathy, cataract, ocular motor palsy, optic neuropathy, or sudden refractive change.

cards.q: What is diabetic papillopathy?
cards.a: Benign bilateral or unilateral optic disc swelling with mild visual loss in (often young type 1) diabetics; usually resolves.

chunks.title: Graves: CAS & NOSPECS
chunks.tldr: Thyroid eye disease (systemic view): may precede hyperthyroidism; also Hashimoto, euthyroid, amiodarone. Antibodies to TPO, thyroglobulin, TSH receptor (target on orbital fibroblasts). Signs: von Graefe lid lag (most characteristic), lid retraction, lagophthalmos, axial proptosis, IR fibrosis (downward eye, IOP rise on upgaze), choroidal folds, SLK, exposure, compressive optic neuropathy; ptosis → MG. CAS (Mourits): 7 initial items — retrobulbar pain, pain on gaze, lid redness, conjunctival redness, chemosis, caruncle swelling, lid oedema; ≥3/7 = active, likely to respond to anti-inflammatories. NOSPECS: No signs, Only signs, Soft tissue, Proptosis, Extraocular muscles, Cornea, Sight loss. Selenium 100 µg bd for mild.
chunks.hook: CAS ≥3 = hot → treat with steroids; cold → surgery when stable.

cards.q: Clinical Activity Score threshold for active TED?
cards.a: 3 or more of the 7 inflammatory signs.

chunks.title: Vitamins & granulomatous disease
chunks.tldr: Vit A: xerophthalmia + rod dysfunction (nyctalopia). Vit E: retinal degeneration. Thiamine (B1): Wernicke (confusion, ataxia, nystagmus, ophthalmoplegia) in alcoholics → IV thiamine first; beriberi optic atrophy. B2 → rosacea-like keratitis; niacin (pellagra) rare optic neuritis; B12 → optic neuropathy; vit C (scurvy) → lid/orbital/subconjunctival haemorrhages. TB: <1% of pulmonary TB, granulomatous panuveitis, choroidal tubercles (miliary), tuberculoma, meningitis palsies. Sarcoid: black patients 10×, granulomatous uveitis, periphlebitis, disc granuloma, choroiditis, lacrimal/parotid (gallium). Eales: young men, peripheral periphlebitis + NV + VH (TB link) — diagnosis of exclusion. Leprosy: cool anterior segment — lagophthalmos (VII), madarosis, corneal anaesthesia, interstitial keratitis, miotic iris pearls.
chunks.hook: Confused alcoholic with nystagmus → thiamine before glucose.

cards.q: Ocular triad of Wernicke encephalopathy?
cards.a: Nystagmus, ophthalmoplegia (often VI/gaze palsy), with confusion and ataxia.

cards.q: Why does leprosy favour the anterior segment?
cards.a: Mycobacterium leprae grows best at cooler temperatures.

chunks.title: Syphilis, toxoplasmosis & herpes viruses
chunks.tldr: Congenital syphilis: late interstitial keratitis, salt-and-pepper chorioretinitis. Acquired: secondary stage — anterior uveitis, vitritis, placoid chorioretinitis, optic neuritis → neurosyphilis regimen. Toxo: cats; usually reactivated congenital; focal retinochoroiditis next to scar; treat only sight-threatening; no periocular steroid; acquired → IgG + IgM. HZO: V1; Hutchinson sign; acutely conjunctivitis, keratitis, scleritis, uveitis, optic neuropathy; oral acyclovir 800 mg 5×/d ×7–10 d within 72 h (famciclovir/valaciclovir); immunocompromised → IV acyclovir 30 mg/kg/d; vaccine for older adults. CMV: CD4 <50–100, haemorrhagic necrotising retinitis; IV ganciclovir/oral valganciclovir induction ×2 wk then maintenance; foscarnet (renal), cidofovir (uveitis, hypotony); stop after CD4 >100–200 for 3 months on HAART. EBV: keratitis, uveitis.
points: Congenital CMV: microphthalmia, cataract, optic atrophy; DDx TORCH.
chunks.hook: CMV: 'pizza-pie' (cheese and ketchup) in a patient with CD4 <50.

cards.q: First-line treatment of CMV retinitis?
cards.a: Induction IV ganciclovir or oral valganciclovir (2–3 weeks), then maintenance; intravitreal ganciclovir for zone 1.

cards.q: Main toxicities of foscarnet and cidofovir?
cards.a: Foscarnet: nephrotoxicity, electrolyte disturbance. Cidofovir: nephrotoxicity, uveitis and hypotony.

chunks.title: ARN, PORN, congenital infections & fungi
chunks.tldr: ARN (healthy hosts; VZV > HSV): anterior uveitis, occlusive arteritis, peripheral confluent necrosis spreading circumferentially fast, vitritis; vitreous PCR; IV acyclovir → oral 3 months (protects fellow eye); intravitreal ganciclovir/foscarnet; RD common. PORN (AIDS, VZV): posterior multifocal outer retinal whitening, little inflammation, very fast, poor outcome. Rubella: bilateral cataract (75%), microphthalmia, salt-pepper retinopathy, glaucoma. Measles: Koplik spots, keratitis. Mumps: dacryoadenitis. Post-MMR bilateral optic neuritis — steroids, recovers. Candida: IV lines, drug users — fluffy chorioretinitis → vitreous 'string of pearls'; intravitreal amphotericin/voriconazole + systemic fluconazole, early vitrectomy. Mucor: DKA, black palate, orbital apex.
chunks.hook: ARN: angry eye, arteritis, advancing ring. PORN: posterior, pale, quiet, quick.

cards.q: Difference between ARN and PORN?
cards.a: ARN: immunocompetent, marked inflammation, peripheral necrosis with arteritis. PORN: immunocompromised (AIDS), minimal inflammation, multifocal posterior outer retinal necrosis, rapid.

cards.q: Classic vitreous appearance of Candida endophthalmitis?
cards.a: Fluffy white vitreous balls in a 'string of pearls'.

chunks.title: HIV/AIDS & Lyme disease
chunks.tldr: Opportunists by CD4: <500 zoster, Candida, TB; <200 Pneumocystis, toxo, cryptococcus; <100 CMV, MAC. Eye involved in ~30–70%: commonest HIV microvasculopathy (CWS, haemorrhages — asymptomatic), conjunctival microvasculopathy, intermediate uveitis (high viral load), CMV retinitis, ARN/PORN, toxo (bilateral, acquired), choroidal Pneumocystis/crypto/MAC (dissemination), severe HZO (in Africa may present HIV), syphilis (severe), molluscum, Kaposi. Immune recovery uveitis after HAART. Rifabutin, cidofovir → uveitis. Lyme (Borrelia, ticks): erythema migrans + conjunctivitis → neuro (VII palsy, III/IV/VI), uveitis, neuroretinitis, keratitis; serology; doxycycline/amoxicillin/ceftriaxone 14 days.

cards.q: Commonest ocular finding in HIV?
cards.a: HIV microvasculopathy — cotton-wool spots and small haemorrhages.

chunks.title: SLE, APS, vasculitides & RA
chunks.tldr: SLE: dry eye (⅓), episcleritis/scleritis, lupus retinopathy (CWS, haemorrhages → severe vaso-occlusion = active CNS/renal disease), lupus choroidopathy (serous RD), optic neuropathy; HCQ retinopathy risk. Antiphospholipid: venous/arterial occlusions, NAION, choroidal infarcts; lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin. PAN: painless scleritis, PUK, retinal vasculitis, CRAO. GPA (Wegener): 50% ocular — orbital mass, NLDO, PUK, necrotising scleritis; c-ANCA (PR3) (only 30% in limited disease); steroids + cyclophosphamide/rituximab. RA: KCS (15%), scleritis (heralds systemic vasculitis), scleromalacia perforans, PUK/melt; TNF inhibitors may worsen eye. Dermatomyositis: heliotrope lids. Scleroderma: tight lids.

cards.q: Typical antibody in granulomatosis with polyangiitis?
cards.a: c-ANCA directed against proteinase 3 (PR3).

cards.q: What does severe vaso-occlusive retinopathy in SLE signal?
cards.a: Active systemic disease, often CNS lupus and antiphospholipid antibodies — poor prognosis.

chunks.title: JIA, Sjögren, GCA, Takayasu, AS & Behçet
chunks.tldr: JIA: oligoarticular girls, ANA+ in 88% with uveitis; quiet chronic anterior uveitis → band keratopathy, synechiae, cataract, glaucoma; screen; MTX. Sjögren: dry eye + mouth, women, anti-Ro/La or labial gland biopsy; risk of lymphoma. GCA: >50 (avg 70), women; jaw claudication, scalp tenderness, PMR; AION/CRAO in 30–60%; ESR/CRP; biopsy; immediate steroids, 1–2 y. Takayasu: young women, aortic arch → pulseless, ocular ischaemic syndrome. Ankylosing spondylitis: young men, HLA-B27 (~90%), recurrent acute AAU in 25–50%. Behçet: oral + genital ulcers, pathergy, thrombosis; ocular 75% — hypopyon panuveitis, occlusive retinal vasculitis, infiltrates; HLA-B51, Silk Road; anti-TNF, interferon, aza, ciclosporin; 25% poor vision.
chunks.hook: Hypopyon that shifts + mouth ulcers + Turkish/Japanese patient = Behçet.

cards.q: HLA associated with Behçet disease?
cards.a: HLA-B51.

cards.q: Ocular manifestation of Takayasu arteritis?
cards.a: Ocular ischaemic syndrome (hypotensive retinopathy) from aortic arch branch stenosis.

chunks.title: Marfan, OI, metabolic disorders, VKH, SJS, rosacea
chunks.tldr: Marfan (FBN1, chr 15, AD; 25% new): tall, arachnodactyly, aortic root; superotemporal lens subluxation, high myopia, RD, megalocornea, glaucoma. Osteogenesis imperfecta (type 1 collagen, AD): fractures, blue sclera, deafness, keratoconus. Wilson (AR): Kayser-Fleischer ring (copper in Descemet), sunflower cataract. Cystinosis (AR): corneal crystals. Albinism: nystagmus, iris TID, foveal hypoplasia, excess chiasmal decussation (VEP). Galactosaemia: oil-droplet cataract. VKH: Asian/Hispanic, bilateral granulomatous panuveitis + exudative RD, then sunset-glow fundus; poliosis, vitiligo, alopecia, tinnitus/meningism; high-dose steroids. SJS/TEN: drugs (allopurinol, carbamazepine), membranous conjunctivitis → cicatrisation; stop drug, amniotic membrane early. Rosacea: MGD, keratitis 5%, doxycycline.
points: Immunosuppressants: steroids, aza, ciclosporin, MMF, MTX, cyclophosphamide, biologics (anti-TNF, IL-6R, IGF-1R for TED) — monitor.
chunks.hook: VKH: Vitiligo, Kinky (white) hair, Hearing loss + bilateral serous detachments.

cards.q: Where is copper deposited in Wilson disease?
cards.a: Peripheral Descemet's membrane (Kayser-Fleischer ring); also anterior capsule (sunflower cataract).

cards.q: Electrophysiological sign of albinism?
cards.a: Asymmetric (crossed) VEP from excessive decussation of optic nerve fibres at the chiasm.
